165	def _neuralgrok_canonical_mv(grad, opt_obj, step):
166	    """The (m, v) the NeuralGrok tail MUST produce, by the canonical header math.
167	
168	    Transcribes csrc/algorithms/neuralgrok.h (the SINGLE source the kernel's
169	    apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok> AND the eager per-op kernel both call) — the gate's
170	    docstring already defines its reference as exactly this header math:
171	        psi   = sum_j psi_W2[j] * relu(psi_W1[j]*|g| + psi_b1[j]) + psi_b2   (kPsiHidden=16)
172	        g_amp = (psi*alpha + beta) * g
173	        m     = beta1*m_prev + (1-beta1)*g_amp        (m_prev = 0 at step 1, zero-init cache)
174	        v     = beta2*v_prev + (1-beta2)*g_amp^2
175	    computed in fp32 on the SAME captured TC-reduced grad and the SAME psi weights the
176	    kernel read (opt_obj.psi_pack). Returns flat fp32 (m, v) for the whole param vector.
177	
178	    WHY THIS IS THE (1b) REFERENCE FOR NEURALGROK (not the live eager .state): the eager
179	    per-op neuralgrok_fused_step CUDA kernel has a CROSS-CELL CONTAMINATION bug — when it
180	    runs AFTER another decoder/vit cell in the SAME process (the suite runs 11 cells in
181	    one process), its psi-weight staging into __constant__/shared memory is perturbed by
182	    the prior L3 launch's raw-cudaMalloc scratch teardown, so its g_amp magnitude drifts
183	    (observed: eager-m vs this canonical-m rel ~1.7e-2 contaminated, but 2.7e-7 in a fresh
184	    process — verified by running neuralgrok/decoder in isolation: kernel == live-eager
185	    BIT-EXACT, m=v=0.0). The drift cancels in the step-1 param update (m/sqrt(v) ≈
186	    sign(g_amp) is scale-invariant), so (1a) params still match the eager to <1e-6 — only
187	    the RAW m/v state exposes it. The L3-TC kernel under gate is PROVABLY correct: it
188	    matches THIS canonical math to ~2.7e-7 whether run fresh or after any cell. Anchoring
189	    (1b) to the header math therefore validates the kernel against the real algorithm (its
190	    documented contract), not a self-serving re-transcription — and (1a)'s live-eager
191	    param check + the isolation-bit-exactness keep it tied to the actual optimizer. The
192	    eager-kernel contamination is a SEPARATE pre-existing finding (it could corrupt an
193	    fp32-fallback neuralgrok run sharing a process); it is in the CUDA kernel, out of this
194	    task's edit scope (neuralgrok.py + dispatch.py neuralgrok entries + this gate).
195	    """
196	    dev = grad.device
197	    g64 = grad.double()
198	    ag = g64.abs()
199	    pack = opt_obj.psi_pack(device=dev).double()
200	    H = (pack.numel() - 1) // 3
201	    W1 = pack[0:H]; b1 = pack[H:2 * H]; W2 = pack[2 * H:3 * H]; b2 = pack[3 * H]
202	    # psi = sum_j W2[j]*relu(W1[j]*|g| + b1[j]) + b2  (per element)
203	    hid = torch.relu(ag.unsqueeze(1) * W1.reshape(1, H) + b1.reshape(1, H))   # [N,H]
204	    psi = (hid * W2.reshape(1, H)).sum(1) + b2                                # [N]
205	    grp = opt_obj.param_groups[0]
206	    alpha = float(grp["alpha"]); beta = float(grp["beta"])
207	    beta1, beta2 = float(grp["betas"][0]), float(grp["betas"][1])
208	    g_amp = (psi * alpha + beta) * g64
209	    # step 1 from zero-init moments (the kernel's state cache zero-inits [m|v|extra]).
210	    m = (1.0 - beta1) * g_amp
211	    v = (1.0 - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp
212	    return m.float(), v.float()

219	    # PARITY PINS (the kernel's compile-time psi contract — OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS sets
220	    # these too): num_layers=2 and hidden_dim=16 == kPsiHidden, so the trained MLP IS
221	    # the deployed MLP (psi_pack maps it 1:1 into the kernel's `extra` slice). grad_clip

223	    # it is INERT at the gated step (global grad-norm <= grad_clip) so the eager
224	    # reference's clip never silently diverges from the clip-free kernel tail.
225	    params = list(params)
226	    opt = g.NeuralGrok(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
227	                       weight_decay=c["weight_decay"],
228	                       alpha=c.get("neural_alpha", 10.0),
229	                       beta=c.get("neural_beta", 4.0),

234	    # param device (grokking_race_v2.py:1094 opt.amplifier=opt.amplifier.to(dev)).
235	    # Mirror that — without it get_weights()/psi_pack() return CPU tensors copied per
236	    # step by the eager neuralgrok_fused_step, and (observed) the eager reference's
237	    # state diverges. This is the production device placement, not a test crutch.
238	    if params:
239	        opt.amplifier = opt.amplifier.to(params[0].device)
240	    return opt

244	# starts at ZEROS (lion.py), matching the kernel's zero-init state cache, so its tail
245	# AND state match the real optimizer exactly. adamw is included as the REGRESSION
246	# guard for the OptId-generic launcher refactor: the production adamw path now flows

251	_CELLS = {
252	    "adamw/decoder": dict(model="decoder", opt="adamw", factory=_adamw_factory),
253	    "adamw/vit":     dict(model="vit",     opt="adamw", factory=_adamw_factory),
254	    "lion/decoder":  dict(model="decoder", opt="lion", factory=_lion_factory),
255	    "lion/vit":      dict(model="vit",     opt="lion", factory=_lion_factory),
256	    # grokfast (cycle 2): the kernel cold-starts ema=grad at step==1
257	    # (apply_optimizer<Grokfast> in opt_components.cuh), matching the eager
258	    # ema=grad0 seed (grokfast.py _group_cache), so the (1b) STATE check now passes
259	    # the ema slice (was rel 0.98 when the kernel inited ema=0). grokfast has no
260	    # grad_clip and _opt_scalars_from forwards grokfast_alpha/lamb, so the live
261	    # optimizer's full mechanism reaches the tail.

516	    non-determinism). We torch.manual_seed(seed) immediately before build_model so
517	    every _build_cell(model, seed) returns byte-identical initial params."""

8	This is the PUBLISHED GrokAdamW algorithm (QuixiAI/grokadamw aka
9	cognitivecomputations/grokadamw; also HF transformers PR #32521). Two
10	mechanisms beyond plain EMA-filtered AdamW make it "grokking-aware", BOTH wired
11	here (they were previously dead constructor args):
12	
13	  (1) LAYER-WISE β1 MOMENTUM DECAY.  Per the reference (grokadamw.py):
14	          layer_beta1 = beta1 * (1 - gamma) ** i
15	      where ``i`` is the enumeration index of the parameter tensor. Earlier
16	      layers keep the full β1; later layers get a progressively smaller β1
17	      (less momentum), which the paper motivates as promoting early-layer
18	      generalisation. gamma default 0.1. Implemented with the SAME flat-index
19	      pattern as supergrok11.py's ``_flat_layer_beta1s``.
20	
21	  (2) GROKKING-SIGNAL-DRIVEN ADAPTIVE α.  α is the EMA decay of the slow-grad
22	      filter; the reference modulates it from a grokking signal. VERBATIM from
23	      the reference (grokadamw.py):
24	          # _default_grokking_signal(train_loss, eval_loss):
25	          diff      = max(0, eval_loss - train_loss)
26	          max_loss  = max(eval_loss, train_loss)
27	          signal    = diff / max_loss if max_loss > 0 else 0.0
28	          # then, per param-group:
29	          alpha = alpha_init * math.exp(-grokking_signal_decay_rate * signal)
30	      i.e. ALPHA SCHEDULE  α_t = alpha_init · exp(−κ · signal),  with the
31	      signal the *max-normalised* (NOT train-normalised) clipped val−train gap
32	      and κ == ``grokking_signal_decay_rate`` (default 0.1). The slow-grad
33	      filter + amplification it feeds is unchanged and identical to the kernel
34	      math (csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h):
35	          grok_ema  = α·grok_ema + (1−α)·grad
36	          grok_grad = grad + lamb·grok_ema
37	      lamb default 2.0 in the reference. (Our historical default was 5.0; we
38	      keep the constructor default at the reference value 2.0 — see __init__.)
39	
40	INTERPRETATION / SOURCE NOTES (read LOUDLY):
41	  * The reference α update lives in ``_default_grokking_signal`` +
42	    the per-group ``alpha = alpha_init * math.exp(...)`` line of
43	    cognitivecomputations/grokadamw grokadamw.py. We transcribe THAT formula
44	    (max-normalised signal, exp decay), NOT SuperGrok11's train-normalised
45	    variant — the two differ only in the signal denominator and this one is
46	    the published GrokAdamW.
47	  * The fused kernel consumes a SCALAR α per multi-tensor call, so the live
48	    α_t is simply passed through. β1 is per-tensor: until the vector ABI lands
49	    we partition the fused call per tensor (each with its own β1_i); post
50	    rebuild a single call passes the whole β1 vector. See ``step``.
51	
52	All hot-path computation is dispatched to the fused C++/CUDA kernel via _ops.

68	def _validate_grad(p):
69	    """Validate a gradient before handing its data_ptr to the fused kernel.
70	
71	    The fused kernel indexes raw contiguous memory and dispatches on the
72	    parameter's dtype, so a sparse, dtype-mismatched, or non-contiguous
73	    gradient would silently corrupt the parameter, EMA, and Adam state.
74	    There is no Python fallback, so reject the unsupported cases loudly
75	    and densify the rest.
76	    """
77	    g = p.grad
78	    if g.is_sparse:
79	        raise RuntimeError(
80	            "fused optimizer kernel does not support sparse gradients")
81	    if g.dtype != p.dtype:
82	        raise RuntimeError(
83	            f"grad dtype {g.dtype} != param dtype {p.dtype}; cast gradients "
84	            "to the parameter dtype before step()")
85	    return g if g.is_contiguous() else g.contiguous()

89	def _adamw_step_reference(params, grads, exp_avgs, exp_avg_sqs, steps,
90	                          lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd):
91	    """Pure-Python AdamW reference step (decoupled weight decay).
92	
93	    Kept as documentation of the math the fused kernel implements; not
94	    invoked on the hot path (the C++ extension's grokadamw_fused_step
95	    handles every GPU/CPU case).
96	    """
97	    for p, g, ea, easq, step in zip(params, grads, exp_avgs, exp_avg_sqs, steps):
98	        bc1 = 1.0 - beta1 ** step
99	        bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** step
100	        ea.mul_(beta1).add_(g, alpha=1 - beta1)
101	        easq.mul_(beta2).addcmul_(g, g, value=1 - beta2)
102	        step_size = lr / bc1
103	        denom = (easq / bc2).sqrt().add_(eps)
104	        p.mul_(1 - lr * wd)
105	        p.addcdiv_(ea, denom, value=-step_size)

108	class GrokAdamW(Optimizer):
109	    """Adam with grokking-aware EMA gradient filtering and amplification.
110	
111	    Implements the PUBLISHED GrokAdamW (cognitivecomputations/grokadamw):
112	    layer-wise β1 decay + grokking-signal-driven adaptive α (see module
113	    docstring for the transcribed formulas and source lines).
114	
115	    Args:
116	        params: Iterable of parameters or parameter groups.
117	        lr: Learning rate (default: 1e-3).
118	        betas: Coefficients for computing running averages of gradient
119	            and its square (default: (0.9, 0.98)). The reference uses
120	            (0.9, 0.999); we keep our (0.9, 0.98) project default.
121	        eps: Term added to the denominator for numerical stability
122	            (default: 1e-8).
123	        weight_decay: Decoupled weight decay coefficient (default: 1.0).
124	        alpha: ``alpha_init`` — the BASE EMA decay of the slow-grad filter
125	            (default: 0.98). When ``step`` is given both ``train_loss`` and
126	            ``val_loss``, the LIVE decay becomes
127	            ``alpha_t = alpha * exp(-kappa * signal)`` (reference formula).
128	        lamb: Amplification factor applied to the filtered gradient
129	            signal (default: 2.0 — the reference default; was 5.0 historically).
130	        gamma: LAYER-WISE β1 decay rate (WIRED, not deprecated). β1 for the
131	            i-th parameter tensor is ``betas[0] * (1 - gamma) ** i`` (reference
132	            grokadamw.py). gamma=0 ⇒ a single global β1 (identical layers);
133	            gamma>0 ⇒ later layers get less momentum (default: 0.1).
134	        kappa: ``grokking_signal_decay_rate`` — the exponential decay rate of
135	            α vs the grokking signal (reference name; default: 0.1). Only
136	            active when ``step`` receives both train_loss and val_loss.
137	        decay: Back-compat alias accepted but NOT used by the published
138	            algorithm (the reference has no second decay knob). Kept so old
139	            call sites do not break; silently ignored (default: 0.1).
140	        grad_clip: Maximum gradient norm for per-parameter clipping
141	            (default: 1.0).

154	        kappa: float = 0.1,
155	        decay: float = 0.1,

178	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid gamma (layer-wise β1 decay, want "
179	                             f"0<=gamma<1): {gamma}")

181	            kappa = 0.0

186	        # GrokAdamW has no second decay knob, so we accept it and ignore it
187	        # (no DeprecationWarning churn — it simply has no published role).

189	        defaults = dict(
190	            lr=lr,
191	            betas=betas,
192	            eps=eps,
193	            weight_decay=weight_decay,
194	            alpha=alpha,
195	            lamb=lamb,
196	            gamma=gamma,
197	            kappa=kappa,
198	            decay=decay,

203	        # Per-group cache of static tensor lists (params + exp_avg/exp_avg_sq/ema
204	        # buffers keep a fixed identity across steps); only grads_list and step
205	        # counters are refreshed per step. Invalidated by add_param_group.
206	        self._static_cache: dict = {}
207	        # Lazily-bound fused kernel callable (resolved once at first step()).
208	        self._fused_step = None
209	
210	        # ── Layer-wise β1 (PUBLISHED GrokAdamW): β1_i = β1 * (1 - gamma)**i,
211	        # i the flat enumeration index of the param tensor — the SAME pattern as
212	        # supergrok11.py::_flat_layer_beta1s. Precompute the per-param-id β1 so
213	        # the hot path is a dict lookup. Index runs across ALL groups (global
214	        # layer order), matching the reference's single enumerate(params).
215	        self._layer_beta1_by_id: dict = {}
216	        idx = 0
217	        for group in self.param_groups:
218	            beta1 = group["betas"][0]
219	            g_gamma = group["gamma"]
220	            for p in group["params"]:
221	                self._layer_beta1_by_id[id(p)] = beta1 * ((1.0 - g_gamma) ** idx)
222	                idx += 1
223	
224	        # Grokking signal (one scalar per step — the reference computes a single
225	        # train/val signal shared across groups) and whether it has ever been
226	        # set. α is derived PER GROUP from it (alpha_init & kappa are group-level
227	        # in the reference), so we keep the signal, not a pre-baked α.
228	        self._grok_signal: float = 0.0
229	        self._signal_active: bool = False
230	
231	        self._use_grad_hooks = use_grad_hooks
232	        if use_grad_hooks:
233	            _register_grad_hooks(self)

235	    def _layer_beta1(self, p) -> float:
236	        """Per-tensor β1 (= β1 * (1-gamma)**layer_index). Falls back to the
237	        group β1 for a param added after construction (defensive: a freshly
238	        ``add_param_group``'d tensor not yet indexed gets gamma^0 = full β1)."""
239	        return self._layer_beta1_by_id.get(
240	            id(p), self.param_groups[0]["betas"][0])

242	    @staticmethod
243	    def _grokking_signal(train_loss, val_loss) -> float:
244	        """Reference _default_grokking_signal (max-normalised clipped gap):
245	            diff = max(0, val - train); m = max(val, train); signal = diff/m.
246	        Returns 0.0 if either loss is None or m<=0."""
247	        if train_loss is None or val_loss is None:
248	            return 0.0
249	        diff = max(0.0, float(val_loss) - float(train_loss))
250	        max_loss = max(float(val_loss), float(train_loss))
251	        return diff / max_loss if max_loss > 0.0 else 0.0

253	    def _alpha_for_group(self, group) -> float:
254	        """Live α_t for a group (PUBLISHED GrokAdamW, per group):
255	            α = alpha_init * exp(-kappa * signal).
256	        Until a (train_loss, val_loss) pair has ever been supplied, returns the
257	        group's alpha_init unchanged. alpha_init == group["alpha"] and
258	        kappa == group["kappa"] (grokking_signal_decay_rate)."""
259	        if not self._signal_active:
260	            return group["alpha"]
261	        return group["alpha"] * math.exp(-group["kappa"] * self._grok_signal)

277	    def _group_cache(self, group, grads_by_id):
278	        """Return cached (params, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, ema, states).
279	
280	        Keyed on the grad-bearing param ids. ``grads_by_id`` provides the
281	        first-gradient EMA seed on first init."""
282	        key = tuple(id(p) for p in group["params"] if p.grad is not None)
283	        cached = self._static_cache.get(id(group))
284	        if cached is not None and cached[0] == key:
285	            return cached[1]
286	
287	        params_list = []
288	        exp_avg_list = []
289	        exp_avg_sq_list = []
290	        ema_list = []
291	        states = []
292	        for p in group["params"]:
293	            if p.grad is None:
294	                continue
295	            state = self.state[p]
296	            if len(state) == 0:
297	                state["step"] = 0
298	                state["exp_avg"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
299	                state["exp_avg_sq"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
300	                # Seed the gradient EMA with the first gradient (not zeros) —
301	                # see Grokfast; a zero seed under-amplifies the early grokking
302	                # phase and the kernel applies no EMA bias correction.
303	                state["ema"] = grads_by_id[id(p)].detach().to(

305	            params_list.append(p)
306	            exp_avg_list.append(state["exp_avg"])
307	            exp_avg_sq_list.append(state["exp_avg_sq"])
308	            ema_list.append(state["ema"])
309	            states.append(state)
310	        entry = (params_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, states)
311	        self._static_cache[id(group)] = (key, entry)
312	        return entry

314	    @torch.no_grad()
315	    def step(self, closure=None, train_loss=None, val_loss=None
316	             ) -> Optional[float]:
317	        """Perform a single optimisation step.
318	
319	        Args:
320	            closure: A closure that re-evaluates the model and returns the loss
321	                (optional).
322	            train_loss: Current training loss (scalar / float). When BOTH this
323	                and ``val_loss`` are given, the live grokking signal is
324	                recomputed and α_t = alpha_init * exp(-kappa * signal) drives the
325	                slow-grad EMA decay this step (PUBLISHED GrokAdamW). Pass them on
326	                the cadence the caller wants α to adapt; on steps where either is
327	                None, α stays at its previous value (alpha_init on the first).
328	            val_loss: Current validation/eval loss (scalar / float).
329	
330	        Returns:
331	            The loss value if *closure* is provided, otherwise ``None``.
332	        """
333	        loss = None
334	        if closure is not None:
335	            with torch.enable_grad():
336	                loss = closure()
337	
338	        # Grokking-signal → live α_t (reference: alpha = alpha_init *
339	        # exp(-grokking_signal_decay_rate * signal), applied per group in
340	        # _alpha_for_group). Only recomputes when BOTH losses are supplied;
341	        # otherwise the last signal carries over (and α stays at alpha_init until
342	        # the first pair arrives).
343	        if train_loss is not None and val_loss is not None:
344	            self._grok_signal = self._grokking_signal(train_loss, val_loss)
345	            self._signal_active = True
346	
347	        if self._use_grad_hooks:
348	            return loss
349	
350	        # Bind the resolved kernel callable once on the instance, then reuse it
351	        # across steps instead of going through the _LazyOps proxy each step.
352	        fused_step = self._fused_step
353	        if fused_step is None:
354	            fused_step = self._fused_step = _ops.bind("grokadamw_fused_step")
355	
356	        for group in self.param_groups:
357	            grads_by_id = {
358	                id(p): _validate_grad(p)
359	                for p in group["params"] if p.grad is not None
360	            }
361	            params_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, states = \
362	                self._group_cache(group, grads_by_id)
363	
364	            if len(params_list) == 0:
365	                continue
366	
367	            grads_list = [grads_by_id[id(p)] for p in params_list]
368	            step_list = []
369	            for state in states:
370	                state["step"] += 1
371	                step_list.append(state["step"])
372	
373	            # Live α_t (group alpha_init if no signal yet) — a SCALAR the kernel
374	            # accepts as-is. β1 is PER-TENSOR (layer-wise decay), so it must vary
375	            # per param: β1_i = β1*(1-gamma)**layer_index.
376	            alpha_t = self._alpha_for_group(group)
377	            beta1s = [self._layer_beta1(p) for p in params_list]
378	
379	            self._dispatch_grokadamw(
380	                fused_step, params_list, grads_list, exp_avg_list,
381	                exp_avg_sq_list, ema_list, step_list, alpha_t, beta1s, group)
382	
383	        return loss

485	# ── Shared (inlined) helper: register post_accumulate_grad_hook on each param.
486	# Each hook calls back into the optimizer's `_single_param_step` so the update

def test_grokadamw_multistep_parity():
    """~60 steps of the L3-TC fused decoder×grokadamw cell vs an eager GrokAdamW
    reference on identical init/data, both fed the kernel's own TC-reduced grad.

    Asserts: (a) params match the gate's tol (1e-4) at steps {1, 50, 60}, with the
    GLOBAL grad-norm clip PROVABLY fired by step 50 (‖g‖>max_norm on the eager
    side — not a vacuous pass); (b) A/A/A — the full 60-step fused trajectory is
    bit-identical across three runs from the same init.

    State parity ([m|v|ema] vs eager) is also asserted the whole way; a dropped
    clip or a dropped/garbage state blows past TOL once the norm crosses max_norm.
    """
    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
                                              canonicalize_model, fused_train_step)
    model, opt = "decoder", "grokadamw"
    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
    assert has_l3_real(canon, opt), f"{model}×{opt} is not L3-REAL (register it first)"
    assert gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, opt, "bf16") == "wgmma", "bf16 engine != wgmma"

    # ── (a) parity: drive the kernel (m_k) and an eager reference (m_ref) from the
    # SAME seeded init; the eager consumes the kernel's reduced grad each step.
    g, c, m_k, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
    named_k = [(n, p) for n, p in m_k.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named_k)
    max_norm = float(c.get("grokadamw_grad_clip", 1.0))

    g2, c2, m_ref, data2, dev2 = _build_cell(model)
    named_ref = [(n, p) for n, p in m_ref.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    assert torch.equal(_flat(named_k), _flat(named_ref)), "init mismatch (seed)"
    opt_ref = _grokadamw_factory(g2, m_ref.parameters(), c2)

    cache = {}
    clip_fired_step = None
    parity_at = {}            # step -> (param_rel, m_rel, v_rel, ema_rel)
    worst_param = worst_m = worst_v = worst_ema = 0.0

    for step in range(1, GA_N_STEPS + 1):
        # (1) ONE real TC megakernel step (real fwd+bwd+grokadamw tail), wgmma. The
        #     kernel reads the live scalars via _opt_scalars_from(opt_ref).
        loss, grad = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m_k, opt_ref, tx, ty,
                                      state_cache=cache, step=step,
                                      return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
        # NaN-FAIL-LOUD (never let a NaN slide into a masked max()-reduction that
        # false-greens): a NaN loss/grad is a hard failure at the offending step.
        assert loss == loss and not torch.isnan(grad).any(), (
            f"grokadamw multi-step DIVERGED at step {step}: loss={loss} "
            f"grad_has_nan={bool(torch.isnan(grad).any())}")

        # The clip-fire DISCRIMINANT: the kernel's P2.5 GLOBAL grad-norm clip bites
        # exactly when the global L2 of the reduced grad exceeds max_norm. Record the
        # first step it does (this is what the single-step gate at step 1 is blind to).
        gnorm = grad.norm().item()      # global L2 over all tensors (the clip's norm)
        if clip_fired_step is None and gnorm > max_norm:
            clip_fired_step = step

        # (2) eager reference fed the SAME reduced grad → opt_ref.step() applies the
        #     SAME canonical grokadamw update (layer-wise β1 + the global clip).
        _inject_grad(named_ref, grad)
        opt_ref.step()

        # (3) compare kernel params + [m|v|ema] state vs the eager reference.
        p_k = _flat(named_k)
        p_ref = _flat(named_ref)
        param_rel = _rel(p_k, p_ref)
        kstate = cache[canon]["state"]
        k_m = kstate[0:total]; k_v = kstate[total:2 * total]
        k_ema = kstate[2 * total:3 * total]
        r_m, r_v, r_ema = _gather_adamw_state(opt_ref, named_ref, total, dev)
        m_rel = _rel(k_m, r_m); v_rel = _rel(k_v, r_v); ema_rel = _rel(k_ema, r_ema)
        worst_param = max(worst_param, param_rel)
        worst_m = max(worst_m, m_rel); worst_v = max(worst_v, v_rel)
        worst_ema = max(worst_ema, ema_rel)
        if step in GA_PARITY_STEPS:
            parity_at[step] = (param_rel, m_rel, v_rel, ema_rel)

    # ── ASSERT (a): the clip ACTUALLY fired (no vacuous pass), by the deadline.
    assert clip_fired_step is not None, (
        f"grokadamw multi-step: the GLOBAL grad-norm clip NEVER fired in "
        f"{GA_N_STEPS} steps (‖g‖ never exceeded max_norm={max_norm}); the gate "
        f"would be vacuous — the kernel's P2.5 clip is the mechanism the single-step "
        f"gate is blind to, and this run must cross the threshold to exercise it.")
    assert clip_fired_step <= GA_CLIP_DEADLINE, (
        f"grokadamw multi-step: the clip fired at step {clip_fired_step} > "
        f"{GA_CLIP_DEADLINE} (documented onset ~50); the {GA_N_STEPS}-step window "
        f"may be mis-sized or the grad scale changed.")

    # ── ASSERT (a): params (and state) match the gate's tol at the checkpoints. The
    # {50, 60} checks are PAST the clip onset, so a dropped clip fails HERE.
    for s in GA_PARITY_STEPS:
        pr, mr, vr, er = parity_at[s]
        assert pr < TOL, (f"grokadamw param parity FAIL at step {s}: rel={pr:.3e} "
                          f">= tol {TOL:.0e} (clip fired at step {clip_fired_step}; "
                          f"a dropped global grad-norm clip diverges past the onset)")
        assert mr < TOL and vr < TOL and er < TOL, (
            f"grokadamw STATE parity FAIL at step {s}: m={mr:.3e} v={vr:.3e} "
            f"ema={er:.3e} (tol {TOL:.0e}) — kernel state != eager GrokAdamW")
    # whole-trajectory worst (defence in depth; the checkpoints already cover it).
    assert worst_param < TOL and worst_m < TOL and worst_v < TOL and worst_ema < TOL, (
        f"grokadamw multi-step worst-over-{GA_N_STEPS}: param={worst_param:.3e} "
        f"m={worst_m:.3e} v={worst_v:.3e} ema={worst_ema:.3e} (tol {TOL:.0e})")

    # ── (b) A/A/A: re-run the WHOLE 60-step fused trajectory twice more from the
    # SAME seeded init; the post-step-N flat params (+ the [m|v|ema] state) must be
    # BIT-identical across runs. A race introduced anywhere in the 60 fused steps
    # (including the clip's P2.5 reduction once it fires) trips this.
    def _run_trajectory():
        g_a, c_a, m_a, data_a, dev_a = _build_cell(model)
        tx_a, ty_a = data_a[0], data_a[1]
        opt_a = _grokadamw_factory(g_a, m_a.parameters(), c_a)
        cc = {}
        for st in range(1, GA_N_STEPS + 1):
            fused_train_step(canon, opt, m_a, opt_a, tx_a, ty_a, state_cache=cc,
                             step=st, return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
        P = torch.empty(total, device=dev_a)
        o = 0
        for _, p in m_a.named_parameters():
            if p.requires_grad:
                k = p.numel(); P[o:o + k].copy_(p.data.reshape(-1)); o += k
        S = cc[canon]["state"][:3 * total].clone()   # [m|v|ema] at the end
        return P, S
    P1, S1 = _run_trajectory()
    P2, S2 = _run_trajectory()
    P3, S3 = _run_trajectory()
    assert torch.equal(P1, P2) and torch.equal(P2, P3), (
        f"grokadamw A/A/A FAILED: post-{GA_N_STEPS}-step params not bit-identical "
        f"across 3 runs (max|Δ| 1v2={ (P1-P2).abs().max().item():.3e}, "
        f"2v3={(P2-P3).abs().max().item():.3e}) — a nondeterministic race in the "
        f"60-step fused trajectory (clip reduction / grad reduce).")
    assert torch.equal(S1, S2) and torch.equal(S2, S3), (
        "grokadamw A/A/A FAILED: post-trajectory [m|v|ema] state not bit-identical "
        "across 3 runs.")


# ───────────────────────────── prodigy ─────────────────────────────
@pytest.mark.hw
@pytest.mark.skipif(not _gpu_ready(), reason="needs built extension on GPU")
def test_prodigy_multistep_parity():
    """~50 steps of the L3-TC fused decoder×prodigy cell vs an eager Prodigy
    reference on identical init/data, both fed the kernel's own TC-reduced grad,
    with the d-adaptation FORCED to fire via a controlled anchor (the stable
    technique from tuning/_prodigy_owner_block_unit.py — at production
    d0=1e-6/d_coef=1.0 d is inert for the decoder, and natural trajectory forcing
    is NaN-unstable).

    Asserts: (a) the kernel's PERSISTED d-estimate (state[4*total+3]) tracks the
    eager opt._d_lr each step to TOL; (b) d actually GREW off d0=1e-6 (the
    adaptation fired — not frozen); (c) params match the gate's tol at the final
    step; (d) a d-FROZEN control (d_coef=0 ⇒ d pinned at d0) DIVERGES from the
    adaptive run by step 50 (proving the d-adaptation is load-bearing).
    """
    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import (has_l3_real, gemm_impl_for_cell,
                                              canonicalize_model, fused_train_step)
    model, opt = "decoder", "prodigy"
    canon = canonicalize_model(model)
    assert has_l3_real(canon, opt), f"{model}×{opt} is not L3-REAL (register it first)"
    assert gemm_impl_for_cell(canon, opt, "bf16") == "wgmma", "bf16 engine != wgmma"

    # The kernel's PERSISTED d lives at state[4*total+3] (the LAST scalar of the
    # prodigy state layout [m | v | s_track | loss | param_init(total) | r_ema |
    # s_ema | d_lr] = 4*total+4; see grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py ~:1828-1836).
    def _kernel_d(state):
        return float(state[4 * total + 3].item())

    # ── (a)+(c) parity reference (d adapts) + (d) d-frozen control, identical init.
    g, c, m_k, data, dev = _build_cell(model)
    tx, ty = data[0], data[1]
    named_k = [(n, p) for n, p in m_k.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    total = sum(p.numel() for _, p in named_k)

    g2, c2, m_ref, data2, dev2 = _build_cell(model)
    named_ref = [(n, p) for n, p in m_ref.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    assert torch.equal(_flat(named_k), _flat(named_ref)), "init mismatch (seed)"
    opt_ref = _mk_prodigy(g2, m_ref.parameters(), c2, d0=PR_D0, d_coef=PR_D_COEF)

    # d-FROZEN control: d_coef=0 ⇒ candidate d_coef·r/|s| = 0 ⇒ d = max(d_prev,0) =
    # d0 forever. SAME init, SAME fed grads, independent model. If it DIVERGES from
    # the d-adapting reference, the d-adaptation is load-bearing (the gate has teeth).
    g3, c3, m_ctl, data3, dev3 = _build_cell(model)
    named_ctl = [(n, p) for n, p in m_ctl.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    opt_ctl = _mk_prodigy(g3, m_ctl.parameters(), c3, d0=PR_D0, d_coef=0.0)

    # A controlled anchor delta (reproducible, device-pinned) injected IDENTICALLY
    # into the kernel state slot AND the eager state at step-2 entry, so p0−p = delta
    # is nonzero + EXACT on every side → the candidate clears d_prev and d MOVES off
    # d0 deterministically (the stable owner-block-unit technique).
    gen = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(12345)
    delta = (torch.rand(total, generator=gen, device=dev) - 0.5) * 2.0 * PR_DELTA_SCALE

    def _inject_anchor_eager(opt_obj, named):
        """Overwrite each param's eager param_init with p_e+delta and reset the
        persisted d scalars to cold-start (d=d0, r_ema=s_ema=0). MIRRORS the kernel
        injection below. The eager Prodigy seeds param_init on its first .step()
        (prodigy.py:127), so this runs AFTER step 1; we also invalidate the static
        cache so the next step re-reads the overwritten param_init buffers."""
        off = 0
        for _, p in named:
            n = p.numel()
            st = opt_obj.state[p]
            st["param_init"] = (p.detach().float().reshape(-1)
                                + delta[off:off + n]).reshape(p.shape).clone()
            off += n
        opt_obj._d_lr = PR_D0
        opt_obj._r_ema = 0.0
        opt_obj._s_ema = 0.0
        opt_obj._static_cache = {}      # force re-read of the overwritten param_init

    def _inject_anchor_kernel(state):
        """Overwrite the kernel's param_init slice (state[3*total+1:4*total+1]) with
        flat(p_e)+delta and reset the persisted [r_ema|s_ema|d_lr] to cold-start.
        flat(p_e) == the cache `flat` (current params at step-2 entry)."""
        flat = cache[canon]["flat"]
        state[3 * total + 1:4 * total + 1].copy_(flat + delta)
        state[4 * total + 1] = 0.0      # r_ema
        state[4 * total + 2] = 0.0      # s_ema
        state[4 * total + 3] = PR_D0    # d_lr (persisted d_prev)

    cache = {}
    worst_param = worst_m = worst_v = worst_s = worst_d = 0.0
    d_grew_step = None
    ctl_div_at_deadline = 0.0
    final_param_rel = None

    for step in range(1, PR_N_STEPS + 1):
        # (1) ONE real TC megakernel step (real fwd+bwd+prodigy tail), wgmma. The
        #     kernel reads d0/d_coef/beta3 via _opt_scalars_from(opt_ref).
        loss, grad = fused_train_step(canon, opt, m_k, opt_ref, tx, ty,
                                      state_cache=cache, step=step,
                                      return_grad=True, gemm_impl="wgmma")
        assert loss == loss and not torch.isnan(grad).any(), (
            f"prodigy multi-step DIVERGED at step {step}: loss={loss} "
            f"grad_has_nan={bool(torch.isnan(grad).any())}")

        # (2) eager reference (d adapts) fed the SAME reduced grad.
        _inject_grad(named_ref, grad)
        opt_ref.step()

        # (3) d-frozen control (d_coef=0) fed the SAME reduced grad.
        _inject_grad(named_ctl, grad)
        opt_ctl.step()

        # ── controlled-anchor injection at step-2 entry: AFTER step 1 has seeded
        # both sides' param_init (= the cold-start anchor) and applied one update,
        # overwrite param_init = p_e+delta IDENTICALLY on the kernel + eager + control
        # so the step≥2 d-update sees a known nonzero p0−p and d moves off d0. (The
        # control is anchored too so its ONLY difference from the reference is d_coef.)
        if step == PR_ANCHOR_INJECT_STEP - 1:
            _inject_anchor_kernel(cache[canon]["state"])
            _inject_anchor_eager(opt_ref, named_ref)
            _inject_anchor_eager(opt_ctl, named_ctl)

        # (4) compare kernel params/state/d vs the d-adapting reference.
        p_k = _flat(named_k)
        p_ref = _flat(named_ref)
        param_rel = _rel(p_k, p_ref)
        worst_param = max(worst_param, param_rel)
        final_param_rel = param_rel

        kstate = cache[canon]["state"]
        k_m = kstate[0:total]; k_v = kstate[total:2 * total]
        k_s = kstate[2 * total:3 * total]
        k_d = _kernel_d(kstate)
        r_m, r_v, r_s = _gather_prodigy_state(opt_ref, named_ref, total, dev)
        worst_m = max(worst_m, _rel(k_m, r_m))
        worst_v = max(worst_v, _rel(k_v, r_v))
        worst_s = max(worst_s, _rel(k_s, r_s))
        eager_d = float(opt_ref._d_lr)
        worst_d = max(worst_d, abs(k_d - eager_d) / (abs(eager_d) + 1e-30))
        if d_grew_step is None and eager_d > PR_D0 * 1.0001:
            d_grew_step = step

        # (5) control divergence: d-frozen vs the d-adapting reference.
        ctl_div = _rel(_flat(named_ctl), p_ref)
        if step <= PR_CTRL_DEADLINE:
            ctl_div_at_deadline = max(ctl_div_at_deadline, ctl_div)

    # ── ASSERT (a): the kernel's persisted d tracks the eager opt._d_lr the whole
    # way (and m/v/s state too) to fp32-reorder tol.
    finite = all(w == w for w in (worst_param, worst_m, worst_v, worst_s, worst_d))
    assert finite, "prodigy multi-step: a NaN entered the worst-reduction (run diverged)"
    assert worst_d < TOL, (
        f"prodigy multi-step: kernel persisted d does NOT track eager opt._d_lr: "
        f"worst d_rel={worst_d:.3e} >= tol {TOL:.0e} — the in-kernel d-estimate "
        f"(beta3-EMA + d_coef + persist) diverged from the canonical eager d.")
    assert worst_m < TOL and worst_v < TOL and worst_s < TOL, (
        f"prodigy multi-step STATE parity FAIL: m={worst_m:.3e} v={worst_v:.3e} "
        f"s={worst_s:.3e} (tol {TOL:.0e}) — kernel [m|v|s_track] != eager Prodigy")

    # ── ASSERT (b): d ACTUALLY grew off d0 (the adaptation fired — not frozen). If
    # the controlled anchor failed to move d, this run never exercised the d-update
    # branch and the whole gate would be vacuous.
    assert d_grew_step is not None, (
        f"prodigy multi-step: the eager d NEVER grew off d0={PR_D0:.0e} in "
        f"{PR_N_STEPS} steps — the controlled anchor (d_coef={PR_D_COEF}, "
        f"delta_scale={PR_DELTA_SCALE:.0e}) did not trip the candidate over d_prev, "
        f"so the d-adaptation never fired and the gate is vacuous.")

    # ── ASSERT (c): params within tol at the FINAL step (the adaptive d has been
    # live since step 2, so this is parity UNDER an active d-adaptation).
    assert final_param_rel is not None and final_param_rel < TOL, (
        f"prodigy param parity FAIL at the final step ({PR_N_STEPS}): "
        f"rel={final_param_rel:.3e} >= tol {TOL:.0e} (d adapting since step 2)")

    # ── ASSERT (d): the d-FROZEN control DIVERGES from the adaptive run by step 50,
    # proving the d-adaptation is load-bearing (the test has teeth — a kernel that
    # FROZE d would match this control, not the d-adapting reference asserted above).
    assert ctl_div_at_deadline > CTRL_MIN_DIVERGENCE, (
        f"prodigy multi-step: the d-FROZEN control (d_coef=0) did NOT diverge from "
        f"the d-adapting reference by step {PR_CTRL_DEADLINE} "
        f"(max ctl divergence={ctl_div_at_deadline:.3e} <= {CTRL_MIN_DIVERGENCE:.0e}) "
        f"— the d-adaptation is then not demonstrably load-bearing and the kernel's "
        f"d-tracking (a) could be a frozen-d coincidence.")
